intro: Welcome to the Earth Information Jukebox. It turns NASA pictures of the Earth into sound. Every note you hear is data: one note for each moment of the data, higher notes for higher values, and faster notes when there is more activity. The soft background pad never changes and has no beat, so any rhythm you hear is the data itself. Press Space to play or pause. Press N for the next visualization. Press E to explore a still frame with your keys. You can also press K and say a command, like zoom in, or say help. Press H at any time to hear all the keys, and V to turn this voice guide off.
keys: Keys. Space: play or pause. N and P: next or previous visualization. E: explore the current frame. L: play the sound legend. D: spoken descriptions on or off. G: switch between the globe and the flat map. Plus and minus: zoom in and out, and zero to reset. M: night mode. V: voice guide on or off. K: speak a command. H: hear these keys again. In Explore: keys one to four choose Point, Row, Column or Box. Arrow keys move. Shift with an arrow moves faster, or resizes the box. Enter plays. I says where you are. A, in the Box tool, selects the whole map. The square brackets step to the previous or next frame. Escape leaves Explore.
explore: Explore. The picture is paused on one frame so you can study it. There are four tools. One, Point: a harp note plays the value under your probe, over a soft tone that glides with it. Higher means more, and silence means no data. Two, Row: a playhead sweeps from west to east, plucking the values as it goes, with a tick every thirty degrees. Three, Column: the same from north to south, with a deeper tick at the equator. Four, Box: scans an area from left to right, where north is higher and louder means more, then reads a summary. In the Box tool, A selects the whole map. Use the arrow keys to move and Enter to play. The square brackets step through time. Escape returns to playback.
ds-sst: Ocean surface temperature from a NASA ocean model, March 2007 to March 2008. One note plays for each sample, about every two seconds. A low note means a cooler ocean on average {tone:low} and a high note a warmer one. {tone:high} When more of the ocean is above twenty eight degrees, the note repeats faster. Hotter hot spots make it louder and brighter. A soft bell marks each new month. Press Space to play, or E to explore a frame.
ds-nightlights: Night lights seen from space, 2012 to 2023, followed by a map of how they changed. Each note is one moment of the video. A low note means little of the map is lit {tone:low} and a high note means much more. {tone:high} More light also makes the note repeat faster. The years move from your left ear to your right. In the change map, a flute on the right means brighter, and a bass on the left means darker. Press Space to play, or E to explore.
ds-lightning: Lightning seen from the International Space Station. Every flash is a plucked hit. Left or right is where it strikes, higher means further north, and louder means bigger, so the rhythm you hear is the lightning itself. A steady note underneath plays three times a second. It is low when storms are mostly in the south {tone:low} and high when they are in the north. {tone:high} Press Space to play, or E to explore.
ds-earth: Earth, NASA's Blue Marble, with country borders and real clouds. This is a still map for exploring, so it opens in Explore. Move the probe with the arrow keys or the mouse and listen to the place. Shallow seas sound like surf, and the deep ocean is a low rumble that gets deeper with the water. Land is a warm tone that rises with height, high mountains add wind, and glaciers shimmer like ice. A soft tick means you crossed a border, and then the country name is spoken. Plus and minus zoom in to read the countries.
ds-aerosols: Aerosols: smoke, dust, sea salt and sulfate in the air around the whole planet on one day in August 2025, from a NASA model. This is a still map for exploring, so it opens in Explore. Move the probe with the arrow keys or the mouse. A low tone means only a little aerosol {tone:low} and a high tone means a lot. {tone:high} Silence means clear air. When the type changes you hear a soft tick, and the new type is spoken. Choose the Box tool with key four, then press A to scan the whole map from west to east.
voice-help: Voice commands. Press K, then say a command. Play, pause, next, or previous. A visualization: ocean, night lights, lightning, aerosols, or Earth. Explore, and done. Point, row, column, box, whole map, and scan. North, south, east, or west, or far north. Next frame, and previous frame. Zoom in, zoom out, and reset zoom. Louder, quieter, faster, and slower. Legend, describe, night mode, and day mode. Where am I. And on the Earth map, go to a country, like go to France. Say repeat to hear the last message again.
